module_title: IMF's Special Drawing Rights (SDR) and World Bank Structure
introduction: At this level, we look at the technical 'currency' used by the IMF and the specific 'windows' through which the World Bank lends money to different types of countries.

core_concepts.title: Special Drawing Rights (SDR)
core_concepts.description: SDR is NOT a physical currency. It is an international reserve asset created by the IMF in 1969. It is often referred to as 'Paper Gold'. Countries use SDRs to supplement their official reserves.

core_concepts.title: The SDR Basket
core_concepts.description:
The value of an SDR is based on a basket of 5 major world currencies: 
1. US Dollar 
2. Euro 
3. Chinese Yuan (Renminbi) - Added in 2016 
4. Japanese Yen 
5. British Pound.

core_concepts.title: The World Bank (IBRD + IDA)
core_concepts.description:
The term 'World Bank' officially refers to two institutions: 
1. IBRD (International Bank for Reconstruction and Development): Lends to middle-income and creditworthy low-income governments at market rates. 
2. IDA (International Development Association): Provides interest-free loans (credits) and grants to the world's 'poorest' countries. It is called the 'Soft Loan Window'.

core_concepts.title: Key Reports and Publications
core_concepts.description:
1. IMF: 'World Economic Outlook' and 'Global Financial Stability Report'. 
2. World Bank: 'World Development Report'. (Note: The 'Ease of Doing Business' report has been discontinued).

important_entities.name: IMF Quota System
important_entities.significance: Unlike the UN (one country, one vote), voting power in the IMF is determined by the 'Quota' a country contributes. The quota is based on the country’s economic size (GDP), openness, and reserves.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A common MCQ: 'Is the Indian Rupee part of the SDR basket?' The answer is 'No'. Only the five currencies mentioned above are part of it.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: IDA = I Don't (ask for) Any interest
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: The IDA provides loans at 0% interest, making it the softest lending window for poor nations.

exam_strategy_tips: Memorize the reports. Match the following: 'World Economic Outlook' always goes with the IMF.
